She also sent the legislature 151 letters about individual bills. We have retrieved 1 of those letters and have not been able to read 1 of them — they are scanned images and we do not yet have text recognition for them. We hold the documents and can link you to them, but we will not say what any of them decided until we have read it.
We read 12 of the 37 executive orders we indexed, and the index continues past what we walked.

gaps.statement: The link we hold for that meeting is Vail Unified School District Governing Board's agenda portal rather than the agenda itself.

The register also links "Jen Anderson for VUSD Board", "Leroy Smith for Vail School Board", "Anastasia 4 Vail Committee" to this office. The county's public transaction search returns no itemized money rows for those committees, and we have not yet been able to read the report documents they filed — so we cannot say what they raised or spent.

Every dollar figure here comes from campaign-finance reports these committees filed with the county. Independent-expenditure reports — money spent by outside groups for or against a candidate, which is not money a campaign received — are a different kind of filing, and we have not yet acquired any for Pima County. That is a gap in our records, not a finding that no outside spending happened.

County filings: this answer includes the Pima County filing officer's committee and itemized records for the resolved body's campaigns. The filing register links committees to an office, not to an individual person.
State filings: we have not linked a verified state filing to this answer about Vail Unified School District Governing Board. That does not establish that none exists.
